# Choosing the Right Sample Size Method {#sec-method-selection}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Learning objectives"}
- Select a method from endpoint, objective and design.
- Identify when the book or calculator does not cover a design.
:::

## The idea

Begin with the primary question rather than the list of formulas. The decision sequence is: **target population → design and sampling unit → primary estimand and outcome scale → estimation or testing → correlation/dependence → method and parameters → recruitment adjustments**. The method must match the planned primary analysis closely enough for planning purposes.

## When and how to apply it

For paired outcomes, cluster randomisation, survival outcomes, repeated measures and prediction-model development, the present calculator does not provide a complete validated method. Referral to design-specific references and appropriate statistical consultation is better than adapting an incompatible formula.

## Teaching case 1 — baseline draft

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Clinical scenario / initial worked example"}
Five scenarios: estimating obesity prevalence, comparing two independent mean HbA1c values, estimating sensitivity, evaluating a survival endpoint and developing a clinical prediction model. Identify which the current modules can address.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Common error"}
Availability of a calculator button does not determine whether a method is valid for a research objective.
:::

## Key message

An unsupported research design needs another method—not a convenient substitute.
